FR-001.statement: Patrons should be able to register for a library membership card and log in securely.

FR-002.statement: Patrons should be able to search the Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) by title, author, ISBN, subject, and keyword.

FR-003.statement: Patrons should be able to view real-time catalog availability, shelf location, and call numbers.

FR-004.statement: Patrons should be able to reserve or place a hold on currently checked-out or in-transit books.

FR-005.statement: Patrons should be able to view their active borrowed items, due dates, renewal counts, and reading history.

FR-006.statement: Patrons should be able to renew eligible borrowed books online before the scheduled due date.

FR-007.statement: Patrons should be able to view outstanding late return fines and make electronic fee payments.

FR-008.statement: Patrons should receive automated notification alerts for upcoming due dates, available hold arrivals, and overdue notices.

FR-009.statement: Patrons should be able to submit purchase recommendations or inter-library loan requests for missing titles.

FR-010.statement: Circulation staff should be able to verify patron membership status, active hold privileges, and fine balances.

FR-011.statement: Circulation staff should be able to check out physical materials by scanning patron cards and book barcodes.

FR-012.statement: Circulation staff should be able to process returned items, inspect material condition, and return items to inventory.

FR-013.statement: The system should automatically calculate late fees for overdue returned items based on membership policy rules.

FR-014.statement: Circulation staff should be able to collect in-person fine payments and print receipt slips.

FR-015.statement: Circulation staff should be able to manage physical reservations and notify patrons when reserved books are staged on hold shelves.

FR-016.statement: Catalogers should be able to add new bibliographic records, assign Dewey Decimal / Library of Congress classifications, and print barcode labels.

FR-017.statement: Catalogers should be able to manage inventory copies, track lost or damaged materials, and decommission obsolete items.

FR-018.statement: The system should track circulation frequency and generate collection utilization reports.

FR-019.statement: Catalogers should be able to conduct periodic physical inventory audits using barcode scanners.

NFR-001.statement: The system should provide secure role-based access control separating patrons, circulation staff, catalogers, and administrators.

NFR-002.statement: Patrons must only access their own borrowing history, reservation queues, and personal information.

FR-020.statement: Administrators should be able to configure loan durations, maximum borrowing limits, renewal rules, and fine rate schedules.

FR-021.statement: Administrators should be able to generate operational reports on patron membership, circulation velocity, and fine collections.

NFR-003.statement: All configuration updates and administrative overrides must be preserved in a system audit log.
